headline: GAAP earnings squeezed, but distributable earnings hold firm
summary_short: GAAP net income fell to $6.6 million (EPS of $0.01) from a $53.5 million pretax base last quarter, as $107.6 million of corporate interest expense and a $34.2 million corporate derivative loss offset strong segment income; Distributable Earnings held at $0.40 per diluted share on $151.5 million total.
summary_long: Corporate-level interest expense ($107.6M) and a $34.2M derivative loss on hedges wiped out otherwise-strong segment income (Commercial & Residential Lending pretax $136.5M), leaving consolidated pretax income of $21.2M and GAAP EPS of $0.01, down from $0.13 q/q and $0.38 y/y. Distributable Earnings, the REIT's non-GAAP payout metric, held near flat at $0.40/diluted share ($151.5M), aided by non-cash equity comp, D&A and credit-loss-provision add-backs. Cash rose to $367.6M (+26.6% q/q) and total assets hit a record $31.8B after $2.5B invested in the quarter ($6.7B through July). Stockholders' equity dipped 2.5% q/q on the $0.48/share dividend and $30M of H1 buybacks. No formal guidance was issued; management said it expects to resolve ~$900M of underperforming assets by year-end.

drivers.explanation: Corporate segment posted a $175.7M pretax loss - mainly $107.6M of corporate interest expense and a $34.2M derivative loss - that absorbed strong Commercial & Residential Lending segment pretax income of $136.5M.
Follows the net income decline; $8.4M of quarterly income was also allocated to non-controlling interests before the $6.6M attributable to common, on a nearly unchanged 366.7M diluted share count.

DE holds up despite the GAAP miss because it excludes non-cash items - equity compensation, depreciation, and reversals of unrealized loan/securities losses - per the company's own reconciliation table.
Cash built up as the company deployed $2.5 billion of new investments in the quarter and $6.7 billion through July, per CEO/CFO comments in the release.
Equity fell q/q as the $0.48/share dividend and $30 million of H1 2026 share buybacks outpaced retained-earnings growth from the modest net income this quarter.
CEO Sternlicht said real estate fundamentals are improving broadly and the company expects to resolve nearly $900 million of underperforming assets by year end.
